archetype.name: Rebuilding Year (third straight at the bottom)
archetype.definition: A 17-65 season that again ranked last on the site. The offense improved, but the defense and rebounding got worse, so the team never stopped losing by double digits.

report.headline: Offense climbed off the floor, the defense fell through it, and the record held still

recap.finish: 17-65, last in the Southeast; missed the postseason after losing its final 10 games
recap.body:
Washington finished 17-65 with a Net Rtg of -11.7, last in the league, and sat 30th of 30 on the site for the third straight year. Nothing about the record was unlucky. The point margin implied 16 wins and the W vs Pt Diff stat was +1, so close games did not cost this team anything. It lost by 11.98 points a game, the worst margin in the league, because its offense ranked 28th and its defense ranked 30th.

The season went badly from the start. A 1-4 October led into a 1-12 November, and the team was 2-16 by the end of that month. December's 6-8 was the best stretch, and January (4-11) and February (4-8) held at roughly the same weak level. Then it collapsed. March went 1-15, April went 0-7, and the season ended on a 16-game losing streak, against a longest winning streak of two. Over the last 10 games the team allowed 131.8 points a game, 6.92 more than its season average. The defense got worse as the year went on.

The gap with last year shows where the team changed. The offensive rating rose from 106.8 (30th) to 111 (28th). 3P % went from 33.5 to 35.9, exactly the league average, and turnovers stayed at the same 13.6 TOV %. The defense moved the other way. DRtg rose from 119.1 to 122.7, 7 points worse than the league. DRB % was 70.2, last in the league, and Opp eFG % was 56.3. Centers did the most damage: opponents' centers scored 4.14 more points and grabbed 1.72 more rebounds against Washington than in their other games, the most in the league on both counts. The extra offense was cancelled out by what the team gave up on the glass and inside.

Every roster group graded in the D range: backcourt D-, wings D, frontcourt D-. The backcourt took the most minutes and returned the least. Its four listed players combined for 1 Win Share. Bub Carrington played all 82 games and had an On-Off of -8.6. Tre Johnson used 22.5% of possessions with a 53.5 TS % and a BPM of -5. The best production came from a few players. Justin Champagnie led the team with 3.1 Win Shares, a 58.9 TS % and a +3.5 On-Off. Alex Sarr was the only regular with a positive BPM (0.7), and Kyshawn George posted a -1.2 BPM, but each of them played only 48 games.

The team lost three more games than last year's 18-64 and posted a slightly better Net Rtg. In practice that means it stood still at the bottom of the league, with the improvement on one end erased by the decline on the other.

highlights.title: Champagnie was the steadiest contributor
highlights.body: Justin Champagnie ranked 26th of 96 at small forward and led the team with 3.1 Win Shares and 384 rebounds. He scored efficiently at a 58.9 TS % and the team was better with him on the floor (+3.5 On-Off). His production came from an efficient, rebounding-heavy role at modest usage, and that kind of profile tends to repeat.

highlights.title: The offense left last place
highlights.body: The offensive rating rose from 106.8, last in the league a year ago, to 111. Much of that came from shooting: 3P % climbed to the league average of 35.9 after 33.5 last season. The offense is still 4.8 points below the league, so this is progress from very bad to bad, but it is real progress.

highlights.title: Sarr's impact when he played
highlights.body: Alex Sarr ranked 27th of 95 at his position. He carried a 25.7 USG % and was the only regular with a positive BPM (0.7). He played only 48 games, so the frontcourt grade reflects how much he was missing as much as how he played.

lowlights.title: Last in defense and on the glass
lowlights.body: The DRtg of 122.7 ranked 30th and was 7 points worse than the league. Underneath it, DRB % (70.2) and REB % (46.7) were both last, and opposing centers posted the league's biggest gains over their own averages. This is a third straight year with a defense ranked 27th or worse, so the problem is structural, not a slump.

lowlights.title: A 1-15 March and 0-10 finish
lowlights.body: After a competitive December, the season fell apart. March went 1-15, April went 0-7, and the team lost its last 10 by 18.1 points a game. In that closing stretch the offense held at its season level while the defense allowed 6.92 more points a game.

lowlights.title: Backcourt minutes, little return
lowlights.body: The backcourt's four listed players logged 6214 minutes and combined for 1 Win Share. Carrington's -8.6 On-Off over all 82 games was the worst on the roster, and Johnson took a large share of possessions at a 53.5 TS %. Unless those players improve, this group grades D- again.

arc.note: The team was 2-16 by the end of November and found a modest level in December (6-8). It then fell away completely, going 1-22 across March and April and ending on 16 straight losses.

recap.nextYear: The 17 wins were not a fluke in either direction. The margin implied 16, so there is no bad luck to expect back. Whatever improvement comes has to come from the defense and the defensive glass, the two worst units in the league and the reason the offensive gains led nowhere. The building blocks in these numbers are Champagnie's efficient, rebounding-heavy play and the stretches with Sarr and George, the team's three best-ranked players. Sarr and George each played only 48 games, so their availability is a major unknown. The backcourt is the biggest problem: it took the most minutes, produced almost no Win Shares, and its every-game starter had the worst On-Off on the team. Anthony Gill's 68.2 TS % in a small role and Jamir Watkins's +6.4 On-Off are minor positives, not foundations.
